name: Mount Everest
overview: The world's highest mountain. Requires prior high-altitude experience, supplemental oxygen planning and extensive permits.

image.alt: Climber in red ascending a snowy mountain peak

name: K2
overview: One of the most technically demanding 8,000 m peaks, with a serious fatality record. Expert-level only.

image.alt: Mountaineer climbing a steep snow slope with a rope

name: Denali
overview: North America's highest peak: extreme cold, glacier travel and heavy loads. NPS registration and fees apply.

image.alt: Mountaineer climbing a snowy slope in winter gear

name: Aconcagua
overview: Highest peak outside Asia. Non-technical by the normal route but a serious high-altitude objective. Permit required.

image.alt: Climber ascending a rugged outdoor rock face

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
overview: A walk-up high-altitude trek where altitude sickness remains the main risk. Park fees and licensed operators required.

image.alt: Mountaineer climbing a snow-covered rocky ridge

name: Mont Blanc
overview: Western Europe's highest summit. Glacier travel, rockfall and fast-changing weather; acclimatization and guiding strongly advised.

image.alt: Climber on a steep alpine rock face

name: Annapurna I
overview: An 8,000-metre Himalayan objective with serious avalanche, weather and altitude hazards. This is an expert mountaineering expedition, not a trekking route.

image.alt: Mountaineer moving across snow and rock on a high mountain

name: Lhotse
overview: The world's fourth-highest mountain lies beside Everest in the Himalaya. Its high-altitude terrain requires extensive expedition experience, acclimatization and current permit information.

image.alt: Mountaineer on a cold-weather snow and ice route

name: Matterhorn
overview: A prominent alpine summit with exposed rock and mixed climbing. Conditions change quickly; route choice and ascent suitability depend on current conditions and the team's technical experience.

image.alt: Climber progressing on a steep alpine rock face
